title: test(plugin-form): object-form `fields` fixtures name fields as strings; the `{ name }` row pins a stored read the declared member refuses (objectui#11550)
body:
Part of #11550
Clause-②: no

Executes item 1 of triage ruling `5969880008` on the code side: the `{ name }` entry in `object-form` `fields` (and the `object-master-detail-form` hand-off) is retired from the authoring faces this PR owns. Item 2, the section "shape 3" inline runtime entry, is not touched. The governed half, the page-builder guide, is a separate draft PR from branch `claude/issue-11550-guide-fields-names-only`. The two land independently, in either order: neither reads the other's files, and the guide example passes every door with or without this PR.

Session: `https://claude.ai/code/session_01FjqrwXPfSMkSfkKYDSRkN2` (os-dev, `mode:subagent` of the PM seat; identity = this branch).

## What changes

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `fieldSecurityPayload.test.tsx` | `FIELDS` = seven `{ name, label }` entries | seven field names. Every dropped `label` equalled the object field's own, and the form never read it |
| `systemManagedPayload.test.tsx` | three `{ name, label }` entries | three names |
| `drawerFirstLoadWindow-10190.test.tsx` | the "flat fields" shape was two `{ name }` entries | `['title', 'note']`. The shape exists to drive the flat (no `sections`) path, not the entry |
| `objectFormFieldsMembers-8071.test.tsx`, row 6 | "tolerates the `{ name }` spelling — recorded as drift, not a second contract" | turned around: the `ObjectFormSchema` zod mirror refuses the entry, with exactly one issue (`invalid_type` at `fields.0`); a bare name is the accepted control; and a STORED entry still draws. The docblock paragraph that recorded the tolerance now records the retirement |
| `topLevelFieldsWarnCoverage-8847.test.tsx` | "`{ name }` is tolerated as the same member as the bare name" | relabelled: the master-detail hand-off keeps the STORED read; not an authoring shape. Same assertion |
| `.changeset/11550-object-form-fields-names-only.md` | none | empty frontmatter: test-only, no package released |

`drawerFirstLoadWindow-10190` is a fixture the claim's list did not name. It was found by re-grepping current `main`, and it is in the claimed class (a fixture that authors `{ name }` field entries).

## The read stays, as stored-value tolerance

`SimpleObjectForm`'s field loop in `ObjectForm.tsx` (the `(fieldName as any).name` arm) and `buildFlatFields` in `flatFields.ts` still draw a `{ name }` entry. The ruling allows it ("A stored `{ name }` entry may stay readable, as objectui#11533 kept stored rules readable"), and measurement shows no stricter door this repo could own:

| Door, measured on `c476be0` (throwaway probe, deleted, never committed) | `fields: [{ name: ... }]` | `fields: ['...']` |
|---|---|---|
| `ObjectFormSchema` zod mirror (declared `string[]`) | refused, `invalid_type` at `fields.0` | accepted |
| authored node via `safeValidateSchema` (the guide's example as written before PR B) | accepted | accepted |
| authored node via `StrictAnyComponentSchema` | accepted | accepted |

The authored node's `properties` bag is `@objectstack/spec`'s `ComponentPropsMap['object-form']` row by reference (objectui#11276), and that row types `fields` members as unknown today. objectui does not narrow a spec row. Triage notes that objectstack-ai/objectstack#21464 types the member as names once its `.objectui-sha` covers this landing. So the authoring door that would refuse the entry is upstream's; this side stops teaching it.

## The ruling's three pins

- **A string `fields` entry draws as before.** Rows 1 to 3 of `objectFormFieldsMembers-8071` and the master-detail member rows are unchanged and green. The respelled fixtures exercise the string path on the default, modal and drawer arms.
- **The guide's `os:check` example parses with names only.** That is PR B; `pnpm check:skill-examples` is green there.
- **The section shape-3 pins stay green.** `submitTargetRefusal.test.tsx` and `sectionFields.test.ts` are untouched and green.

## Ablation (one-shot, from the committed state, restored)

Both legs ran through `ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor must hit once, landing proven by count and blob hash) inside a script with an EXIT/INT/TERM restore trap. The tests import `../ObjectForm` and `@object-ui/types/zod`, which the root vitest config aliases to source, so neither leg needed a rebuild.

- **Leg A, the read.** In `ObjectForm.tsx`, `(fieldName as any).name` was replaced by `undefined`: anchor 1 to 0, blob `2ae1112530f5` to `5e6d5e79185d`. `objectFormFieldsMembers-8071` + `topLevelFieldsWarnCoverage-8847` gave `Tests  2 failed | 13 passed (15)`, exactly the two stored-read rows. Restored: blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **Leg B, the declared side.** In the mirror, `fields: z.array(z.string())` was widened to `z.array(z.unknown())`: anchor 1 to 0, blob `360b2e65b15e` to `7aeed09ef049`. The same two files gave `Tests  1 failed | 14 passed (15)`, row 6 only (`expected [] to deeply equal [ { code: 'invalid_type', … } ]`). Restored the same way.

- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/plugin-form^...' build`: exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. `--listFilesOnly` on the test config lists all five edited test files, among 162 test files.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-form/`: `Test Files  162 passed (162)`, `Tests  1859 passed | 1 skipped (1860)`.
- The five edited files plus the two shape-3 pins: 104 of 104 passed before the edit (BASE `c476be0`) and after it.
- Gates, each exit 0: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check-changeset-presence` (one empty-frontmatter changeset), `check:changeset-claims`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`. `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on all six paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- ESLint, narrowed to the five edited files: 0 errors (25 `no-explicit-any` warnings, none added). Population: all five are inside eslint's own config (`--print-config` resolves each), and `--format json` reports 5 files. Invariance: `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem, so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. The full `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **Authoring faces outside this claim, not edited, reported to the seat.** The published registration descriptions in `packages/plugin-form/src/index.tsx` still say "`{ name }` is tolerated" for the `fields` input of `object-form`, `view:form` and `embeddable-form`, and "(`{ name }` tolerated)" for `object-master-detail-form`. The console warning text in `warnUnresolvedTopLevelField` (`sectionFields.ts`) says "(`{ name }` is tolerated)". These still teach the entry. `index.tsx` is held by objectui#11536 in flight, so it is not edited here. The respelling is to drop each parenthetical, with a changeset, since `src/` text ships.
- `FlatFieldsContext.fields` in `flatFields.ts` documents the `{ name }` read. It is not exported from the package entry, and it describes the read that stays, so it is left as it is.
- objectui#11536 (`index.tsx`, the console parity test) and objectui#11512 (`MasterDetailForm.i18nLabels.test.tsx`) touch none of these files.
